items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage:
Kingston wakes slowly at the roadside diner,
where Errol orders for his son without asking
and Hemi lets him, the way one lets weather happen.
All morning on the hill road the father led,
his old knees steady as a pair of oars,
until, a stone's throw from the painted line,
he bent to fix a shoe that needed no fixing.
Now Hemi turns the ribbon in his fingers
and says the shoe was tied. Errol says, eat.
Hemi does not eat. He watches the hands
that taught him how to grip a cricket bat,
how to lose a game without kicking the dust,
and thinks there must be a way to lose
that costs a man more than winning would.
Outside, a truck of breadfruit idles at the pump,
its driver singing to no one in particular.
items.question: Which choice best describes Hemi's attitude toward his father?
options: Grateful for the victory and eager to celebrate it with Errol
Suspicious that Errol was too tired to finish the race
Indifferent to the race and absorbed in the morning meal
Irritated by the gesture yet moved by what it cost Errol
items.explanation: Hemi는 아버지가 필요 없는 신발 끈을 고친 척하며 일부러 졌다고 지적하고 음식도 먹지 않아 불쾌함을 드러낸다. 그러나 자신에게 바르게 지는 법을 가르친 손을 바라보며, 지는 것이 이기는 것보다 더 큰 대가를 치를 수 있다고 생각하는 데서 아버지의 희생에 대한 감동이 읽힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 리본을 만지는 장면에 기대지만 축하하려는 기색이 없고, B는 신발이 이미 묶여 있었다는 Hemi의 말과 맞지 않으며, C는 Hemi가 음식을 먹지 않고 아버지를 지켜보는 태도를 무시한다.

items.passage: After eleven months under Bogdan's roof, I, Bronislaw, could list his habits the way other boys listed saints: the pencil behind the left ear, the refusal to sand before noon, the low whistle when a board surprised him. That spring he drove us to a salt flat beyond Tbilisi to gather planks bleached by the wind, and while we ate he passed me a photograph of a wardrobe he had made as a young man. Its doors did not meet. I laughed before I could stop myself, and he laughed too, longer than I did. On the drive home I kept the photograph on my knee. I had thought his skill was something he had been handed, like the color of his eyes. In the workshop that week I found myself measuring every cut twice, and once, for no reason I could name, a third time. Bogdan noticed and said nothing, though he moved his own pencil to the right ear.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Bogdan?
options: Admiring, and newly aware his skill was earned
Amused, and less impressed by his old work
Envious, and anxious to equal his reputation
Doubtful, and wary of trusting his judgment
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 Bogdan의 습관을 성인 목록처럼 외울 만큼 그를 존경한다. 맞지 않는 옷장 사진을 본 뒤 화자는 그의 기술이 눈 색깔처럼 타고난 것이라 여겼던 생각을 돌아보고, 이후 치수를 두 번 세 번 재며 그를 본받으려 한다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면 A가 정답이다. B는 화자가 웃은 장면을 근거로 삼지만 존경이 줄었다는 근거는 없고, C와 D는 각각 명성에 대한 경쟁심과 불신을 지어낸 것이다.

items.passage: "Read me the part about the rent again, Cyrus." Mabel had walked her brother out to the soccer field behind their shop, where boys chased a ball through the Manchester dusk. Cyrus read the landlord's letter in Polish, which only he could follow, and said the man would wait until summer. Mabel nodded. Later, folding the page, she saw a date circled in ink, three weeks off, and the word their mother used to write on unpaid bills. All winter, she realized, Cyrus had answered every supplier and every caller himself and reported only easy news. She did not speak. On the field a boy in a red cap missed an open goal and lay down laughing in the wet grass.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how two siblings walked to a soccer field and read a letter
To show how the shop's failure has caused the siblings to quarrel bitterly
To show Mabel recognizing that Cyrus has softened hard news for her
To suggest that people should always tell one another the plain truth
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: Cyrus는 편지를 집주인이 여름까지 기다려 준다고 번역하지만, Mabel은 3주 뒤 날짜와 어머니가 미납 청구서에 쓰던 단어를 발견한다. 이어 겨울 내내 Cyrus가 모든 연락을 혼자 받고 쉬운 소식만 전했다는 사실을 깨닫는다. 두 단서를 합치면 지문의 목적은 C이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 남매가 다투는 장면이 없어 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Amelie and Matthias had shared the music room in Marseille for nineteen years, and in that time their conversations had shrunk to nods across the piano lids. Everyone in the city called him the great teacher, the one whose pupils always won. In March, clearing a cabinet, Amelie found the scores those winning pupils had played. The fingerings in the margins were in her own hand, penciled during lunches she had long since stopped remembering, and clipped to them was a card from Matthias, never sent, thanking her. She sat a while on the piano bench. So his fame stood partly on her forgotten afternoons, she thought, and he had known all along. When he came in, she held out the card. He read it, folded it once, and put it in his breast pocket. A pigeon walked the length of the windowsill and back.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “his fame stood partly on her forgotten afternoons” most nearly suggests that
options: Matthias won his fame by teaching pupils during the afternoons Amelie was away
Amelie regretted the many afternoons she had spent clearing out the cabinet
Matthias's fame in the city was based on rumors that Amelie had forgotten
Matthias's success relied partly on small help Amelie had given and overlooked
items.explanation: Amelie는 우승한 학생들의 악보 여백에 자기 손으로 쓴 운지법이 있고, 그것이 점심시간에 써 두고 잊어버린 것임을 발견한다. Matthias의 부치지 않은 감사 카드는 그가 이 도움을 알고 있었음을 보여 준다. 두 단서를 연결하면 그의 명성이 일부 Amelie가 잊은 도움 위에 서 있다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 오후라는 단어를 시간표로, B는 캐비닛 정리로, C는 명성을 소문으로 잘못 연결한 오답이다.

items.passage: Dhaka's river docks are where I first knew Vikram, as the cook on a cargo ship who kept his galley so quiet you could hear the rice settle. Decades later he became the gardener for the house Janelle bought, and she asked him often about the family who had sold it in such a hurry. He talked instead about aphids and rain. I learned the truth from a neighbor: the old owner's son had borrowed from the wrong people, and the sale had saved him. Vikram knew this too. His silence was a lid pressed down on a simmering pot, and he kept his hand on it through every one of Janelle's questions. When she finally stopped asking, he planted a row of marigolds along the side gate, where the old man used to sit. On the ship, I remember, he had scrubbed the same dented pan every evening until it shone.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a lid pressed down on a simmering pot” most nearly suggests
options: Vikram's struggle to hide his own anger at Janelle's prying questions
Vikram's steady effort to keep a painful family secret from spreading
Vikram's lasting habit of treating every task like work in a galley
Vikram's private wish to tell Janelle the truth about the old owner
items.explanation: 이웃을 통해 옛 주인의 아들이 위험한 빚을 졌다는 사실이 드러나고, Vikram도 이를 알고 있었다. 그는 Janelle의 질문마다 진딧물과 비 이야기로 화제를 돌리며 계속 침묵을 지키는데, 이는 끓는 냄비 뚜껑을 누르듯 비밀이 새어 나가지 않게 막는 행동이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 '끓는'을 분노로, C는 부엌 배경을 문자 그대로, D는 침묵을 털어놓고 싶은 욕구로 잘못 해석했다.

items.passage: Gravel and the dry rattle of reeds: that is what I remember of the riverbed outside Busan where Edith took me each autumn. The ferry had crossed there once, before the river wandered east, and her husband had gone down with it. On the tenth year I, Nikos, came armed with plans for candles, a hired singer, a stone with his name cut deep. Edith listened, then walked out onto the cracked mud and knelt where the channel had been. She traced its old curve with one finger, the banks still plain after all that time. The water leaves, but the shape stays, she said, and put a single pebble in her pocket. I folded my plans into smaller and smaller squares. Up on the road, a boy was selling roasted chestnuts from a cart with one squeaking wheel.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the water leaves, but the shape stays” most nearly suggests that
options: the river may one day return to its old channel near the ferry crossing
Edith expects the river to carve a deeper channel in the coming years
the immediate rush of grief passes, but the loss leaves a lasting mark
a quiet ritual will be remembered longer than any carved stone marker
items.explanation: Edith는 남편을 잃은 지 10년이 된 날 강이 흐르던 자리의 옛 물길을 손가락으로 따라 그리며 강둑이 여전히 뚜렷하다는 것을 보여 준다. 물은 떠났지만 형태가 남았다는 말은 이 장면과 연결되어, 슬픔의 격렬함은 지나가도 상실의 흔적은 남는다는 뜻이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 강을 문자 그대로 해석했고, D는 Nikos의 계획과 비교하는 소재를 썼지만 구절의 의미가 아니다.

items.passage: Vermont's spring melt had put three inches of water in Efua's cellar overnight, and Ciara came down the stairs in borrowed boots, complaining from the first step. "Thirty years at sea and you build a boat in a basement," she said. "Next you'll keep fish in the attic." Efua, who had once captained ore carriers, held up a lantern and let her talk. Ciara listed the damage cheerfully: the soaked boxes, the furnace, the drowned paint cans. Then she reached the hull on its sawhorses, twelve years in the making and still missing half its planks, and her voice dropped. The water had lifted it, barely, off its stands. Ciara stood still, then crouched and set her palm on its side the way one touches a sleeping horse. Upstairs, a kettle began to whistle and kept whistling.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
options: It moves from mild worry to sharp frustration as Ciara discovers the full extent of the flood.
It moves from lively curiosity to quiet sadness as the women accept the boat is ruined.
It moves from playful mockery to hushed awe as Ciara sees the half-built boat afloat.
It moves from tense silence to open relief as Efua finds the furnace has survived.
items.explanation: 초반에 Ciara는 지하실에서 배를 만든다고 Efua를 놀리며 피해 목록조차 유쾌하게 늘어놓는다. 그러나 미완성 선체에 다가가자 목소리가 낮아지고, 물이 선체를 받침대에서 살짝 띄운 것을 보고 잠든 말을 만지듯 조심스레 손을 얹는다. 두 지점을 비교하면 C가 정답이다. A는 피해 목록을 근거로 하지만 분노가 없고, B는 배가 망가졌다는 근거가 없으며, D는 처음부터 침묵이 아니었다.

items.passage: Chalk dust, the stutter of a ceiling fan, and the warm smell of the photocopier filled the back row of the language school in Mumbai, where Sharda and Noa had sat since moving from Pune. They kept a running list of the teacher's favorite phrases in the margins of their worksheets and awarded points whenever he used one. In August Sharda caught a fever and missed nine days. When she returned, Noa was cheerful as ever, though she now borrowed paper from the girl in front and claimed her notebook was at home. On Friday Sharda opened her own bag and found the notebook there. Every lesson she had missed was copied inside in Noa's small slanted letters, the vocabulary underlined in green. Sharda closed it without reading further and sat holding it on her lap. Down the corridor, someone was dragging a desk across the floor.
items.question: Which choice best describes a shift in tone in the passage?
options: It moves from anxious unease to calm confidence as Sharda catches up on her lessons.
It moves from friendly rivalry to open resentment as Noa keeps her notebook hidden.
It moves from careful description to pointed mockery of the teacher's favorite phrases.
It moves from lighthearted fun to silent gratitude as Sharda realizes what Noa did.
items.explanation: 지문 전반부는 두 친구가 선생님의 말버릇에 점수를 매기는 장난스러운 분위기다. 후반부에서 Sharda는 Noa가 공책이 집에 있다고 둘러대며 종이를 빌려 썼던 이유를 깨닫는데, 자신이 결석한 수업이 모두 그 공책에 옮겨 적혀 있었기 때문이다. 공책을 닫고 무릎에 올려 둔 채 말없이 있는 모습은 조용한 감사로 읽힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 따라잡기, B는 숨긴 공책, C는 선생님 말버릇이라는 소재를 잘못 활용했다.

items.passage:
Three rules for the lamp room above the Saône:
trim the wick, log every barge by name,
and let no gossip climb the stairs.

Camille has kept the first two for thirty years.
The third she broke this week, when the ferryman
told her what the café told him: that Talon,
packing for Paris, had said he was glad to go.

She logs the barges. She trims the wick.
She does not ask, at supper, if it is true.
Talon talks of trains, of borrowed books,
and she answers like a ledger, one line each.

Near midnight he climbs up with two cups,
sets one beside the logbook, says nothing,
and writes his own name under the last barge,
then, smaller, a date in early June.

She reads it the way she reads the weather.
Then she lets the lamp turn once, unwatched,
and pours the tea before it cools.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the poem?
options: It shifts from clipped, guarded restraint to quiet tenderness after Talon signs the log.
It shifts from calm routine to open hurt after Camille confronts Talon about the rumor.
It shifts from cheerful pride in Camille's work to anxiety about her son's departure.
It shifts from bitterness toward Talon to resigned acceptance that he will not return.
items.explanation: 소문을 들은 뒤 Camille은 질문하지 않고 '장부처럼 한 줄씩' 대답하며 규칙적인 일만 반복해 절제되고 경계하는 어조를 보인다. 이후 Talon이 장부에 자기 이름과 6월 날짜를 적자, 그녀는 등불을 지켜보지 않고 돌게 두고 차를 따르며 어조가 부드러워진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 그녀가 직접 따지지 않으므로 틀리고, C는 처음부터 즐거운 자부심이 드러나지 않으며, D는 6월 날짜가 귀가를 암시하므로 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Who had seen it first? Layla put the question to the depot clerk, to the driver, to a woman still holding her ticket stub, and each of them answered at once. The case had slid from the rack when the bus braked outside the Beirut depot; or a boy had knocked it; or it had never been latched. Sigrid, who had come to meet her pupil off the bus, listened without interrupting, her mouth set as it was whenever Layla rushed a passage. By the fourth telling the truth had become a coin passed through too many hands, its face rubbed smooth, still spendable but no longer readable. Layla remembered the clasps clicking shut, or remembered wanting to. Sigrid lifted the violin, turned the cracked bridge toward the light, and said that the instrument at least would not lie to them. Then she asked Layla to play an open A, and they both listened.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a coin passed through too many hands” most nearly suggests that the truth
options: had been deliberately bent by witnesses who wanted to seem important
was still being repeated but had lost the details that made it clear
had cost Layla more than she could afford to spend on repairs
had grown more valuable each time another person retold it
items.explanation: 목격자마다 서로 다른 설명을 내놓았고, 네 번째로 전해질 때쯤 진실은 '면이 닳아 여전히 쓸 수는 있지만 읽을 수 없는' 동전처럼 되었다고 서술된다. 또 Layla조차 걸쇠를 잠갔는지 확신하지 못한다. 따라서 이야기는 계속 오가지만 구별되는 세부를 잃었다는 B가 정답이다. A는 의도적 왜곡의 근거가 없고, C는 동전을 실제 비용으로 오해한 것이며, D는 가치가 커졌다는 정반대 해석이다.

items.passage: Rivals rarely make good counselors. Dainius and I learned this at four in the morning in my aunt Kaya's bakery in Albuquerque, where we had played each other across a folding table for eleven years and had never once agreed on an opening. That morning the board stayed in its box. My younger brother had lost every game of his first season and had asked us both, separately, whether to quit. Dainius thought he should hear that he played too fast; I thought he should hear that he would improve. Neither of us said so at first. Between the cooling racks we circled the question like two kings in an endgame, each offering a small remark and then retreating from it, wary of standing anywhere the other could pin down. Kaya, shaping dough, asked whether we planned to decide before the bread did. By the first tray of conchas we had settled only one point: my brother deserved a single answer, not two.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “circled the question like two kings in an endgame” most nearly suggests that the narrator and Dainius
options: had stripped the question down to its simplest remaining elements
were too tired to speak plainly so early in the bakery morning
competed openly to show who understood the brother better
approached the issue warily, each avoiding a committed position
items.explanation: 두 사람은 처음에 각자의 생각을 말하지 않았고, 작은 말을 꺼냈다가 곧 물러서며 상대에게 '붙잡히지 않을' 자리를 피했다고 서술된다. 체스 종반의 두 킹처럼 서로 조심스럽게 거리를 재는 모습이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 종반에 말이 적다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만 지문은 문제를 단순화한 것이 아니라 회피한 것을 강조한다. B의 피로나 C의 공개적 경쟁은 지문의 근거와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: A bus ticket, folded twice, is what I kept. For two years I taught Solange at a school in the hills above Marseille, and for two years she did not speak in class, though the essays she handed in ran for pages, fierce and crowded in pencil. Genevieve, who taught her mathematics, said the girl answered sums the same way: correctly, and in silence. On her last afternoon, before her family moved north, Solange and I waited at the mountain bus stop. I had rehearsed a few sentences about how one ought to say goodbye, and found I could not use any of them. When the bus came she pressed the ticket into my palm. On the back was a single line of thanks, the pencil pushed so hard it had nearly gone through: a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb. I read it on the walk down, and again at my desk that evening.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb” most nearly suggests that
options: the brief note carried the force of everything Solange had left unsaid
the note was cramped because Solange had written it hastily at the stop
Solange preferred written exchanges to the speeches her teacher prepared
the line of thanks was too faint and small to be read with any ease
items.explanation: Solange는 2년 동안 수업에서 말하지 않았지만 글은 길고 강렬했으며, 마지막 날 남긴 한 줄은 종이가 뚫릴 만큼 눌러 쓴 것이었다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면, 엄지 폭의 짧은 글에 말하지 못한 모든 것이 담겼다는 A가 정답이다. B는 '좁다'는 표면 의미만 본 오답이고, C는 교사의 연설과 비교하는 내용이 없으며, D는 세게 눌러 썼다는 서술과 반대된다.

items.passage: When the buffet doors opened, the wedding hall in Busan dissolved into a hundred conversations, and Sunja let the noise carry her to a corner table. Joon, her grandson, slid in beside her, tugging at a collar his mother had ironed too stiffly. He was laughing about the cousin who had tripped on the aisle runner, and Sunja laughed too, swatting his wrist for being unkind. Then he drew a creased photograph from his jacket: a young woman in a borrowed hanbok, standing beside a man no one in the family had ever named. Sunja's hand stopped above her plate. Around them the hall went on clapping for the couple, but at the corner table the air had thinned. She studied the face she had once worn and did not reach for the picture. Joon, sensing he had opened something he could not close, set his chopsticks down without a sound. Somewhere a microphone squealed, and the master of ceremonies announced the cake.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From nostalgic reverence for a wedding custom to open resentment toward the relatives who arranged it
From anxious uncertainty about a family gathering to relieved delight once a missing relative is identified
From formal politeness between near strangers to warm familiarity after the two discover a shared memory
From playful teasing between relatives to a hushed unease after an unexplained image is revealed
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Joon과 Sunja는 넘어진 사촌 이야기로 함께 웃고 손목을 치며 장난스럽게 대화한다. 사진이 나온 뒤 Sunja의 손이 멈추고 '공기가 희박해졌다', Joon이 소리 없이 젓가락을 내려놓는 등 조용하고 불편한 분위기로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 결혼 관습에 대한 경외나 원망이 없고, B는 사진 속 남자가 끝내 밝혀지지 않으며, C는 두 사람이 처음부터 가까운 가족이라 맞지 않다.

items.passage: Who goes to the cinema in Tromso in May, when the sun refuses to set and no one needs the dark? Anders asked himself this as he bought a ticket from a girl reading a magazine. Inside, the theater held eleven people, and one of them was Anneke, who had not come to Mass in three years. She waved with the cheerful ease of someone meeting her dentist at a party, and Anders sat two seats away, pleased by the coincidence. They traded jokes about the stale popcorn. Then Anneke's daughter leaned across her mother's lap. "Why don't we go to church anymore?" she asked. "You said it was because Father Anders moved away." Anneke looked at the blank screen. Anders looked at his ticket stub, folding it into smaller and smaller squares, and neither of them answered. When the lights finally dimmed, both seemed grateful for the advertisements.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It shifts from lighthearted banter between two acquaintances to strained silence once a child exposes an excuse.
It shifts from quiet suspicion between a priest and a parishioner to open reconciliation prompted by a child.
It shifts from irritation at a nearly empty theater to amusement at a child's misunderstanding of a sermon.
It shifts from solemn reflection on the northern summer to cheerful anticipation of the film about to begin.
items.explanation: 처음에 Anneke는 쾌활하게 손을 흔들고 두 사람은 눅눅한 팝콘에 대해 농담을 주고받는다. 그러나 딸이 신부가 이사 갔다는 엄마의 핑계를 드러내자 두 사람은 대답하지 못하고 화면과 표만 바라보는 어색한 침묵에 빠진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 화해가 일어나지 않고, C는 설교에 대한 오해가 아니며, D는 광고를 반기는 것이 기대가 아니라 침묵에서 벗어난 안도이므로 틀리다.

items.passage:
"Sell it," Yaa says, stirring sugar into his glass,
and laughs, and orders bread for both of us,
as if the house were only one more bill
the waiter could clear away with the cups.
Ama, he says, my name a coin he flips,
you still owe me for the ticket here.
The trains come in. The trains go out.
Then he is quiet, looking at the board,
at a town whose name was once his father's,
and the jokes go out of his hands like steam.
He says the roof leaked even when we were boys.
He says it softly, the way one says a prayer
one is not sure one still believes.
Outside, a porter sings to a cart of melons.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone over the course of the text?
options: It moves from bitter accusation about an unpaid debt to forgiving warmth toward a relative.
It moves from breezy, joking practicality about a sale to subdued and wistful reflection.
It moves from nervous excitement about a journey to calm acceptance of a delayed train.
It moves from reverent nostalgia for a family house to brisk impatience with the waiter.
items.explanation: 초반의 Yaa는 웃으며 집을 치워 버릴 계산서처럼 여기고 조카의 빚을 동전 던지듯 가볍게 언급한다. 중반 이후 그는 말이 없어지고 아버지의 고향 이름을 바라보며 농담이 김처럼 빠져나가고, 지붕 이야기를 기도처럼 조용히 말한다. 따라서 가벼운 실용적 태도에서 차분하고 아련한 회상으로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 빚을 쓰라리게 비난하지 않으며, C와 D는 여행의 흥분이나 웨이터에 대한 조급함이 지문에 없다.

items.passage: We took the letters to the bridge because the apartment was already full of boxes. Mathis, my sister, read the first one aloud in a mock-theatrical voice, and I applauded each of our mother's complaints about the price of leeks, the neighbor's dog, the rain over the Saone. "Etienne, listen to this one," she would say, and bow before reading. For half an hour it felt like a performance staged for two. Then she opened a letter dated the spring before she was born, and her voice dropped. Our mother had written that she was afraid of staying in Lyon forever, afraid she would never see the sea again. Mathis folded the page along its old crease. I thought of her plane ticket, tucked into the passport in her coat, and of how she had mentioned it to me as if mentioning the weather. Below us the river carried a single plastic bottle past the pillars, turning it slowly, never letting it sink.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone of the text changes?
options: From grief over a mother's death to relief that the letters contain no painful secrets
From weary resentment about packing to excited curiosity about the mother's early life
From playful amusement at ordinary details to a sober recognition tied to a departure
From quiet confusion about old letters to firm agreement about where the family should live
items.explanation: 처음에 Mathis는 과장된 연극조로 편지를 읽고 화자는 대파 값이나 이웃집 개 같은 사소한 불평에 박수를 친다. 그러다 어머니가 리옹에 갇힐까 두려워했다는 편지가 나오자 목소리가 낮아지고, 화자는 떠날 준비를 마친 동생의 비행기표를 떠올린다. 따라서 장난스러운 즐거움에서 떠남과 연결된 진지한 깨달음으로 바뀐다는 C가 정답이다. A의 안도, B의 짐 싸기에 대한 원망, D의 합의는 지문에 근거가 없다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-06-058 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Kingston wakes slowly at the roadside diner,
where Errol orders for his son without asking
and Hemi lets him, the way one lets weather happen.
All morning on the hill road the father led,
his old knees steady as a pair of oars,
until, a stone's throw from the painted line,
he bent to fix a shoe that needed no fixing.
Now Hemi turns the ribbon in his fingers
and says the shoe was tied. Errol says, eat.
Hemi does not eat. He watches the hands
that taught him how to grip a cricket bat,
how to lose a game without kicking the dust,
and thinks there must be a way to lose
that costs a man more than winning would.
Outside, a truck of breadfruit idles at the pump,
its driver singing to no one in particular.

[질문] Which choice best describes Hemi's attitude toward his father?
A) Grateful for the victory and eager to celebrate it with Errol
B) Suspicious that Errol was too tired to finish the race
C) Indifferent to the race and absorbed in the morning meal
D) Irritated by the gesture yet moved by what it cost Errol

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
Hemi는 아버지가 필요 없는 신발 끈을 고친 척하며 일부러 졌다고 지적하고 음식도 먹지 않아 불쾌함을 드러낸다. 그러나 자신에게 바르게 지는 법을 가르친 손을 바라보며, 지는 것이 이기는 것보다 더 큰 대가를 치를 수 있다고 생각하는 데서 아버지의 희생에 대한 감동이 읽힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 리본을 만지는 장면에 기대지만 축하하려는 기색이 없고, B는 신발이 이미 묶여 있었다는 Hemi의 말과 맞지 않으며, C는 Hemi가 음식을 먹지 않고 아버지를 지켜보는 태도를 무시한다.
### lit40-medium-06-059 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
After eleven months under Bogdan's roof, I, Bronislaw, could list his habits the way other boys listed saints: the pencil behind the left ear, the refusal to sand before noon, the low whistle when a board surprised him. That spring he drove us to a salt flat beyond Tbilisi to gather planks bleached by the wind, and while we ate he passed me a photograph of a wardrobe he had made as a young man. Its doors did not meet. I laughed before I could stop myself, and he laughed too, longer than I did. On the drive home I kept the photograph on my knee. I had thought his skill was something he had been handed, like the color of his eyes. In the workshop that week I found myself measuring every cut twice, and once, for no reason I could name, a third time. Bogdan noticed and said nothing, though he moved his own pencil to the right ear.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Bogdan?
A) Admiring, and newly aware his skill was earned
B) Amused, and less impressed by his old work
C) Envious, and anxious to equal his reputation
D) Doubtful, and wary of trusting his judgment

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 처음에 Bogdan의 습관을 성인 목록처럼 외울 만큼 그를 존경한다. 맞지 않는 옷장 사진을 본 뒤 화자는 그의 기술이 눈 색깔처럼 타고난 것이라 여겼던 생각을 돌아보고, 이후 치수를 두 번 세 번 재며 그를 본받으려 한다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면 A가 정답이다. B는 화자가 웃은 장면을 근거로 삼지만 존경이 줄었다는 근거는 없고, C와 D는 각각 명성에 대한 경쟁심과 불신을 지어낸 것이다.
### lit40-medium-06-061 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
"Read me the part about the rent again, Cyrus." Mabel had walked her brother out to the soccer field behind their shop, where boys chased a ball through the Manchester dusk. Cyrus read the landlord's letter in Polish, which only he could follow, and said the man would wait until summer. Mabel nodded. Later, folding the page, she saw a date circled in ink, three weeks off, and the word their mother used to write on unpaid bills. All winter, she realized, Cyrus had answered every supplier and every caller himself and reported only easy news. She did not speak. On the field a boy in a red cap missed an open goal and lay down laughing in the wet grass.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To recount how two siblings walked to a soccer field and read a letter
B) To show how the shop's failure has caused the siblings to quarrel bitterly
C) To show Mabel recognizing that Cyrus has softened hard news for her
D) To suggest that people should always tell one another the plain truth

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Cyrus는 편지를 집주인이 여름까지 기다려 준다고 번역하지만, Mabel은 3주 뒤 날짜와 어머니가 미납 청구서에 쓰던 단어를 발견한다. 이어 겨울 내내 Cyrus가 모든 연락을 혼자 받고 쉬운 소식만 전했다는 사실을 깨닫는다. 두 단서를 합치면 지문의 목적은 C이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 남매가 다투는 장면이 없어 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-06-073 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Amelie and Matthias had shared the music room in Marseille for nineteen years, and in that time their conversations had shrunk to nods across the piano lids. Everyone in the city called him the great teacher, the one whose pupils always won. In March, clearing a cabinet, Amelie found the scores those winning pupils had played. The fingerings in the margins were in her own hand, penciled during lunches she had long since stopped remembering, and clipped to them was a card from Matthias, never sent, thanking her. She sat a while on the piano bench. So his fame stood partly on her forgotten afternoons, she thought, and he had known all along. When he came in, she held out the card. He read it, folded it once, and put it in his breast pocket. A pigeon walked the length of the windowsill and back.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “his fame stood partly on her forgotten afternoons” most nearly suggests that
A) Matthias won his fame by teaching pupils during the afternoons Amelie was away
B) Amelie regretted the many afternoons she had spent clearing out the cabinet
C) Matthias's fame in the city was based on rumors that Amelie had forgotten
D) Matthias's success relied partly on small help Amelie had given and overlooked

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
Amelie는 우승한 학생들의 악보 여백에 자기 손으로 쓴 운지법이 있고, 그것이 점심시간에 써 두고 잊어버린 것임을 발견한다. Matthias의 부치지 않은 감사 카드는 그가 이 도움을 알고 있었음을 보여 준다. 두 단서를 연결하면 그의 명성이 일부 Amelie가 잊은 도움 위에 서 있다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 오후라는 단어를 시간표로, B는 캐비닛 정리로, C는 명성을 소문으로 잘못 연결한 오답이다.
### lit40-medium-06-075 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Dhaka's river docks are where I first knew Vikram, as the cook on a cargo ship who kept his galley so quiet you could hear the rice settle. Decades later he became the gardener for the house Janelle bought, and she asked him often about the family who had sold it in such a hurry. He talked instead about aphids and rain. I learned the truth from a neighbor: the old owner's son had borrowed from the wrong people, and the sale had saved him. Vikram knew this too. His silence was a lid pressed down on a simmering pot, and he kept his hand on it through every one of Janelle's questions. When she finally stopped asking, he planted a row of marigolds along the side gate, where the old man used to sit. On the ship, I remember, he had scrubbed the same dented pan every evening until it shone.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a lid pressed down on a simmering pot” most nearly suggests
A) Vikram's struggle to hide his own anger at Janelle's prying questions
B) Vikram's steady effort to keep a painful family secret from spreading
C) Vikram's lasting habit of treating every task like work in a galley
D) Vikram's private wish to tell Janelle the truth about the old owner

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
이웃을 통해 옛 주인의 아들이 위험한 빚을 졌다는 사실이 드러나고, Vikram도 이를 알고 있었다. 그는 Janelle의 질문마다 진딧물과 비 이야기로 화제를 돌리며 계속 침묵을 지키는데, 이는 끓는 냄비 뚜껑을 누르듯 비밀이 새어 나가지 않게 막는 행동이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 '끓는'을 분노로, C는 부엌 배경을 문자 그대로, D는 침묵을 털어놓고 싶은 욕구로 잘못 해석했다.
### lit40-medium-06-076 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Gravel and the dry rattle of reeds: that is what I remember of the riverbed outside Busan where Edith took me each autumn. The ferry had crossed there once, before the river wandered east, and her husband had gone down with it. On the tenth year I, Nikos, came armed with plans for candles, a hired singer, a stone with his name cut deep. Edith listened, then walked out onto the cracked mud and knelt where the channel had been. She traced its old curve with one finger, the banks still plain after all that time. The water leaves, but the shape stays, she said, and put a single pebble in her pocket. I folded my plans into smaller and smaller squares. Up on the road, a boy was selling roasted chestnuts from a cart with one squeaking wheel.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “the water leaves, but the shape stays” most nearly suggests that
A) the river may one day return to its old channel near the ferry crossing
B) Edith expects the river to carve a deeper channel in the coming years
C) the immediate rush of grief passes, but the loss leaves a lasting mark
D) a quiet ritual will be remembered longer than any carved stone marker

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Edith는 남편을 잃은 지 10년이 된 날 강이 흐르던 자리의 옛 물길을 손가락으로 따라 그리며 강둑이 여전히 뚜렷하다는 것을 보여 준다. 물은 떠났지만 형태가 남았다는 말은 이 장면과 연결되어, 슬픔의 격렬함은 지나가도 상실의 흔적은 남는다는 뜻이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 강을 문자 그대로 해석했고, D는 Nikos의 계획과 비교하는 소재를 썼지만 구절의 의미가 아니다.
### lit40-medium-06-082 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Vermont's spring melt had put three inches of water in Efua's cellar overnight, and Ciara came down the stairs in borrowed boots, complaining from the first step. "Thirty years at sea and you build a boat in a basement," she said. "Next you'll keep fish in the attic." Efua, who had once captained ore carriers, held up a lantern and let her talk. Ciara listed the damage cheerfully: the soaked boxes, the furnace, the drowned paint cans. Then she reached the hull on its sawhorses, twelve years in the making and still missing half its planks, and her voice dropped. The water had lifted it, barely, off its stands. Ciara stood still, then crouched and set her palm on its side the way one touches a sleeping horse. Upstairs, a kettle began to whistle and kept whistling.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the passage?
A) It moves from mild worry to sharp frustration as Ciara discovers the full extent of the flood.
B) It moves from lively curiosity to quiet sadness as the women accept the boat is ruined.
C) It moves from playful mockery to hushed awe as Ciara sees the half-built boat afloat.
D) It moves from tense silence to open relief as Efua finds the furnace has survived.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
초반에 Ciara는 지하실에서 배를 만든다고 Efua를 놀리며 피해 목록조차 유쾌하게 늘어놓는다. 그러나 미완성 선체에 다가가자 목소리가 낮아지고, 물이 선체를 받침대에서 살짝 띄운 것을 보고 잠든 말을 만지듯 조심스레 손을 얹는다. 두 지점을 비교하면 C가 정답이다. A는 피해 목록을 근거로 하지만 분노가 없고, B는 배가 망가졌다는 근거가 없으며, D는 처음부터 침묵이 아니었다.
### lit40-medium-06-083 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Chalk dust, the stutter of a ceiling fan, and the warm smell of the photocopier filled the back row of the language school in Mumbai, where Sharda and Noa had sat since moving from Pune. They kept a running list of the teacher's favorite phrases in the margins of their worksheets and awarded points whenever he used one. In August Sharda caught a fever and missed nine days. When she returned, Noa was cheerful as ever, though she now borrowed paper from the girl in front and claimed her notebook was at home. On Friday Sharda opened her own bag and found the notebook there. Every lesson she had missed was copied inside in Noa's small slanted letters, the vocabulary underlined in green. Sharda closed it without reading further and sat holding it on her lap. Down the corridor, someone was dragging a desk across the floor.

[질문] Which choice best describes a shift in tone in the passage?
A) It moves from anxious unease to calm confidence as Sharda catches up on her lessons.
B) It moves from friendly rivalry to open resentment as Noa keeps her notebook hidden.
C) It moves from careful description to pointed mockery of the teacher's favorite phrases.
D) It moves from lighthearted fun to silent gratitude as Sharda realizes what Noa did.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문 전반부는 두 친구가 선생님의 말버릇에 점수를 매기는 장난스러운 분위기다. 후반부에서 Sharda는 Noa가 공책이 집에 있다고 둘러대며 종이를 빌려 썼던 이유를 깨닫는데, 자신이 결석한 수업이 모두 그 공책에 옮겨 적혀 있었기 때문이다. 공책을 닫고 무릎에 올려 둔 채 말없이 있는 모습은 조용한 감사로 읽힌다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 따라잡기, B는 숨긴 공책, C는 선생님 말버릇이라는 소재를 잘못 활용했다.
### lit40-medium-06-084 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Three rules for the lamp room above the Saône:
trim the wick, log every barge by name,
and let no gossip climb the stairs.

Camille has kept the first two for thirty years.
The third she broke this week, when the ferryman
told her what the café told him: that Talon,
packing for Paris, had said he was glad to go.

She logs the barges. She trims the wick.
She does not ask, at supper, if it is true.
Talon talks of trains, of borrowed books,
and she answers like a ledger, one line each.

Near midnight he climbs up with two cups,
sets one beside the logbook, says nothing,
and writes his own name under the last barge,
then, smaller, a date in early June.

She reads it the way she reads the weather.
Then she lets the lamp turn once, unwatched,
and pours the tea before it cools.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the poem?
A) It shifts from clipped, guarded restraint to quiet tenderness after Talon signs the log.
B) It shifts from calm routine to open hurt after Camille confronts Talon about the rumor.
C) It shifts from cheerful pride in Camille's work to anxiety about her son's departure.
D) It shifts from bitterness toward Talon to resigned acceptance that he will not return.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
소문을 들은 뒤 Camille은 질문하지 않고 '장부처럼 한 줄씩' 대답하며 규칙적인 일만 반복해 절제되고 경계하는 어조를 보인다. 이후 Talon이 장부에 자기 이름과 6월 날짜를 적자, 그녀는 등불을 지켜보지 않고 돌게 두고 차를 따르며 어조가 부드러워진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 그녀가 직접 따지지 않으므로 틀리고, C는 처음부터 즐거운 자부심이 드러나지 않으며, D는 6월 날짜가 귀가를 암시하므로 지문과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-07-012 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Who had seen it first? Layla put the question to the depot clerk, to the driver, to a woman still holding her ticket stub, and each of them answered at once. The case had slid from the rack when the bus braked outside the Beirut depot; or a boy had knocked it; or it had never been latched. Sigrid, who had come to meet her pupil off the bus, listened without interrupting, her mouth set as it was whenever Layla rushed a passage. By the fourth telling the truth had become a coin passed through too many hands, its face rubbed smooth, still spendable but no longer readable. Layla remembered the clasps clicking shut, or remembered wanting to. Sigrid lifted the violin, turned the cracked bridge toward the light, and said that the instrument at least would not lie to them. Then she asked Layla to play an open A, and they both listened.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a coin passed through too many hands” most nearly suggests that the truth
A) had been deliberately bent by witnesses who wanted to seem important
B) was still being repeated but had lost the details that made it clear
C) had cost Layla more than she could afford to spend on repairs
D) had grown more valuable each time another person retold it

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
목격자마다 서로 다른 설명을 내놓았고, 네 번째로 전해질 때쯤 진실은 '면이 닳아 여전히 쓸 수는 있지만 읽을 수 없는' 동전처럼 되었다고 서술된다. 또 Layla조차 걸쇠를 잠갔는지 확신하지 못한다. 따라서 이야기는 계속 오가지만 구별되는 세부를 잃었다는 B가 정답이다. A는 의도적 왜곡의 근거가 없고, C는 동전을 실제 비용으로 오해한 것이며, D는 가치가 커졌다는 정반대 해석이다.
### lit40-medium-07-014 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Rivals rarely make good counselors. Dainius and I learned this at four in the morning in my aunt Kaya's bakery in Albuquerque, where we had played each other across a folding table for eleven years and had never once agreed on an opening. That morning the board stayed in its box. My younger brother had lost every game of his first season and had asked us both, separately, whether to quit. Dainius thought he should hear that he played too fast; I thought he should hear that he would improve. Neither of us said so at first. Between the cooling racks we circled the question like two kings in an endgame, each offering a small remark and then retreating from it, wary of standing anywhere the other could pin down. Kaya, shaping dough, asked whether we planned to decide before the bread did. By the first tray of conchas we had settled only one point: my brother deserved a single answer, not two.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “circled the question like two kings in an endgame” most nearly suggests that the narrator and Dainius
A) had stripped the question down to its simplest remaining elements
B) were too tired to speak plainly so early in the bakery morning
C) competed openly to show who understood the brother better
D) approached the issue warily, each avoiding a committed position

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
두 사람은 처음에 각자의 생각을 말하지 않았고, 작은 말을 꺼냈다가 곧 물러서며 상대에게 '붙잡히지 않을' 자리를 피했다고 서술된다. 체스 종반의 두 킹처럼 서로 조심스럽게 거리를 재는 모습이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 종반에 말이 적다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만 지문은 문제를 단순화한 것이 아니라 회피한 것을 강조한다. B의 피로나 C의 공개적 경쟁은 지문의 근거와 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-07-015 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
A bus ticket, folded twice, is what I kept. For two years I taught Solange at a school in the hills above Marseille, and for two years she did not speak in class, though the essays she handed in ran for pages, fierce and crowded in pencil. Genevieve, who taught her mathematics, said the girl answered sums the same way: correctly, and in silence. On her last afternoon, before her family moved north, Solange and I waited at the mountain bus stop. I had rehearsed a few sentences about how one ought to say goodbye, and found I could not use any of them. When the bus came she pressed the ticket into my palm. On the back was a single line of thanks, the pencil pushed so hard it had nearly gone through: a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb. I read it on the walk down, and again at my desk that evening.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a whole conversation squeezed into the width of a thumb” most nearly suggests that
A) the brief note carried the force of everything Solange had left unsaid
B) the note was cramped because Solange had written it hastily at the stop
C) Solange preferred written exchanges to the speeches her teacher prepared
D) the line of thanks was too faint and small to be read with any ease

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
Solange는 2년 동안 수업에서 말하지 않았지만 글은 길고 강렬했으며, 마지막 날 남긴 한 줄은 종이가 뚫릴 만큼 눌러 쓴 것이었다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면, 엄지 폭의 짧은 글에 말하지 못한 모든 것이 담겼다는 A가 정답이다. B는 '좁다'는 표면 의미만 본 오답이고, C는 교사의 연설과 비교하는 내용이 없으며, D는 세게 눌러 썼다는 서술과 반대된다.
### lit40-medium-07-021 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
When the buffet doors opened, the wedding hall in Busan dissolved into a hundred conversations, and Sunja let the noise carry her to a corner table. Joon, her grandson, slid in beside her, tugging at a collar his mother had ironed too stiffly. He was laughing about the cousin who had tripped on the aisle runner, and Sunja laughed too, swatting his wrist for being unkind. Then he drew a creased photograph from his jacket: a young woman in a borrowed hanbok, standing beside a man no one in the family had ever named. Sunja's hand stopped above her plate. Around them the hall went on clapping for the couple, but at the corner table the air had thinned. She studied the face she had once worn and did not reach for the picture. Joon, sensing he had opened something he could not close, set his chopsticks down without a sound. Somewhere a microphone squealed, and the master of ceremonies announced the cake.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From nostalgic reverence for a wedding custom to open resentment toward the relatives who arranged it
B) From anxious uncertainty about a family gathering to relieved delight once a missing relative is identified
C) From formal politeness between near strangers to warm familiarity after the two discover a shared memory
D) From playful teasing between relatives to a hushed unease after an unexplained image is revealed

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
앞부분에서 Joon과 Sunja는 넘어진 사촌 이야기로 함께 웃고 손목을 치며 장난스럽게 대화한다. 사진이 나온 뒤 Sunja의 손이 멈추고 '공기가 희박해졌다', Joon이 소리 없이 젓가락을 내려놓는 등 조용하고 불편한 분위기로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 결혼 관습에 대한 경외나 원망이 없고, B는 사진 속 남자가 끝내 밝혀지지 않으며, C는 두 사람이 처음부터 가까운 가족이라 맞지 않다.
### lit40-medium-07-022 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Who goes to the cinema in Tromso in May, when the sun refuses to set and no one needs the dark? Anders asked himself this as he bought a ticket from a girl reading a magazine. Inside, the theater held eleven people, and one of them was Anneke, who had not come to Mass in three years. She waved with the cheerful ease of someone meeting her dentist at a party, and Anders sat two seats away, pleased by the coincidence. They traded jokes about the stale popcorn. Then Anneke's daughter leaned across her mother's lap. "Why don't we go to church anymore?" she asked. "You said it was because Father Anders moved away." Anneke looked at the blank screen. Anders looked at his ticket stub, folding it into smaller and smaller squares, and neither of them answered. When the lights finally dimmed, both seemed grateful for the advertisements.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) It shifts from lighthearted banter between two acquaintances to strained silence once a child exposes an excuse.
B) It shifts from quiet suspicion between a priest and a parishioner to open reconciliation prompted by a child.
C) It shifts from irritation at a nearly empty theater to amusement at a child's misunderstanding of a sermon.
D) It shifts from solemn reflection on the northern summer to cheerful anticipation of the film about to begin.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
처음에 Anneke는 쾌활하게 손을 흔들고 두 사람은 눅눅한 팝콘에 대해 농담을 주고받는다. 그러나 딸이 신부가 이사 갔다는 엄마의 핑계를 드러내자 두 사람은 대답하지 못하고 화면과 표만 바라보는 어색한 침묵에 빠진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 화해가 일어나지 않고, C는 설교에 대한 오해가 아니며, D는 광고를 반기는 것이 기대가 아니라 침묵에서 벗어난 안도이므로 틀리다.
### lit40-medium-07-023 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
"Sell it," Yaa says, stirring sugar into his glass,
and laughs, and orders bread for both of us,
as if the house were only one more bill
the waiter could clear away with the cups.
Ama, he says, my name a coin he flips,
you still owe me for the ticket here.
The trains come in. The trains go out.
Then he is quiet, looking at the board,
at a town whose name was once his father's,
and the jokes go out of his hands like steam.
He says the roof leaked even when we were boys.
He says it softly, the way one says a prayer
one is not sure one still believes.
Outside, a porter sings to a cart of melons.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone over the course of the text?
A) It moves from bitter accusation about an unpaid debt to forgiving warmth toward a relative.
B) It moves from breezy, joking practicality about a sale to subdued and wistful reflection.
C) It moves from nervous excitement about a journey to calm acceptance of a delayed train.
D) It moves from reverent nostalgia for a family house to brisk impatience with the waiter.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
초반의 Yaa는 웃으며 집을 치워 버릴 계산서처럼 여기고 조카의 빚을 동전 던지듯 가볍게 언급한다. 중반 이후 그는 말이 없어지고 아버지의 고향 이름을 바라보며 농담이 김처럼 빠져나가고, 지붕 이야기를 기도처럼 조용히 말한다. 따라서 가벼운 실용적 태도에서 차분하고 아련한 회상으로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 빚을 쓰라리게 비난하지 않으며, C와 D는 여행의 흥분이나 웨이터에 대한 조급함이 지문에 없다.
### lit40-medium-07-024 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
We took the letters to the bridge because the apartment was already full of boxes. Mathis, my sister, read the first one aloud in a mock-theatrical voice, and I applauded each of our mother's complaints about the price of leeks, the neighbor's dog, the rain over the Saone. "Etienne, listen to this one," she would say, and bow before reading. For half an hour it felt like a performance staged for two. Then she opened a letter dated the spring before she was born, and her voice dropped. Our mother had written that she was afraid of staying in Lyon forever, afraid she would never see the sea again. Mathis folded the page along its old crease. I thought of her plane ticket, tucked into the passport in her coat, and of how she had mentioned it to me as if mentioning the weather. Below us the river carried a single plastic bottle past the pillars, turning it slowly, never letting it sink.

[질문] Which choice best describes how the tone of the text changes?
A) From grief over a mother's death to relief that the letters contain no painful secrets
B) From weary resentment about packing to excited curiosity about the mother's early life
C) From playful amusement at ordinary details to a sober recognition tied to a departure
D) From quiet confusion about old letters to firm agreement about where the family should live

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
처음에 Mathis는 과장된 연극조로 편지를 읽고 화자는 대파 값이나 이웃집 개 같은 사소한 불평에 박수를 친다. 그러다 어머니가 리옹에 갇힐까 두려워했다는 편지가 나오자 목소리가 낮아지고, 화자는 떠날 준비를 마친 동생의 비행기표를 떠올린다. 따라서 장난스러운 즐거움에서 떠남과 연결된 진지한 깨달음으로 바뀐다는 C가 정답이다. A의 안도, B의 짐 싸기에 대한 원망, D의 합의는 지문에 근거가 없다.
